sentences: The programme will give selected software companies technical advice, commercial support, and access to Microsoft and NVIDIA networks to help them develop artificial intelligence products and reach more customers.

Microsoft and NVIDIA have opened applications for Frontier Launchpad, a programme designed to help software companies in the UK and Ireland develop artificial intelligence (AI) products and turn them into sustainable businesses.
The programme builds on last year’s Agentic Launchpad and is aimed at companies with an established software product that are investing in AI or building products around it.
Selected businesses will receive technical advice, commercial guidance, and opportunities to connect with potential customers and partners.

As more organisations add AI to products, day-to-day processes and customer services, the programme will support companies building AI applications, task-specific AI assistants, or software platforms built around AI.

Technical expertise – Participants will work with Microsoft AI specialists, cloud architects, Microsoft Marketplace advisers, and NVIDIA technical experts to develop their products and use AI effectively.

Commercial support – Companies will receive guidance on preparing products for Microsoft Marketplace – the company’s online store for business technology – and on co-selling, where Microsoft and a partner work together to reach new customers.

Commenting on the launch, Tobias Halloran, director of start-ups, Europe, Middle East, Africa and India, NVIDIA, said: “The UK and Ireland have a deep pool of talent building with AI.

Through NVIDIA Inception and the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute, the Frontier Launchpad will give these companies access to NVIDIA’s technical expertise and training to help them build and accelerate their AI applications.”
NVIDIA Inception supports start-ups with technical resources, while the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute provides training in AI and related technologies.
Darren Hardman, CEO, Microsoft UK & Ireland, said: “The UK & Ireland are home to some of the world’s most innovative software companies.

For a start-up selling into regulated financial services, it has been hugely impactful.”
